{{Quote|And as for you, you hyperthyroid whooping crane, should you interfere in my wishes concerning the good captain here, after you have been plucked and roasted, I shall stuff a cushion with your feathers and rest my fundament upon it for the remainder of my life. '''Quor'sav''', or '''Quor'savs''', were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of warm-blooded [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] with both [[Bird/Legends|avian]] and [[monotreme]] characteristics. Their stilt legs and long necks made them tower over most other species at 3.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height. Quor'sav were more vulnerable to illnesses and pollutants than many other species. They laid [[Egg/Legends|eggs]], which took over a year to hatch, and the females often took on a motherly persona when around friends and youth.

The Quor'sav were native to the planet [[Uaua/Legends|Uaua]] in the [[Ua system]] of the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]]. They had a history of poor relations with alien species. At one point, mammalian colonists introduced a virus to Uaua that was deadly to avian biology. As a result, the Quor'sav came to distrust and shun non-avians on their homeworld. During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]], Quor'sav were forced into [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] service as tribute to the galactic government. [[Waywa Fybot]] became a narcotics agent in this manner. [[Kal'Falnl C'ndros]], on the other hand, operated as an independent trader. Due to their unique appearance, Quor'sav were often subjected to insults from members of other species.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|The anatomy is somewhat differently arranged than one might anticipate. That was, believe it or not, a clean shot through the creature's heart.|Rokur Gepta, upon killing Waywa Fybot with a shot through the abdomen|<ref name="classification" />}}
Quor'sav or Quor'savs<ref name="Star Wars: The Saga Collection">Only [[Star Wars: The Saga Collection]] uses ''Quor'savs'' for the plural form.</ref> were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of large, warm-blooded [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]]<ref name="CSWE I 132" /> with characteristics of both [[Bird/Legends|avians]] and [[monotreme]] [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]].<ref name="classification" /> Their birdlike natures were more pronounced, manifest in both their appearance and biology. They had a fragile constitution, much like that of a [[canary]].<ref name="LCATFOO" /> In fact, members of the species who lived on worlds with high levels of air pollution were at risk for respiratory diseases such as [[dioxo-brionchiectasis shock]], [[hemorrhagic molting]], [[lungrot]], and [[silicalung]].<ref name="HNN49">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|life/13328_4.html|Study: Pollution Standards Still Endanger Many}}</ref> Rather than sitting on their posteriors or reclining on their backs like many other species, Quor'sav perched. A certain perching posture brought on a sleep reflex and compelled the Quor'sav to fall into a deep slumber during which they were prone to vivid dreams and, at least in some specimens, snoring. Among the adaptations unique to their species was their heart being located in the abdomen.<ref name="LCATFOO" />

Most non-Quor'sav found the species' appearance bizarre. For one, Quor'sav were larger than most sentient lifeforms, and their bodies demanded extra room for ease of movement.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> Even shorter Quor'sav towered as high as 2.5 meters,<ref name="CSWE I 300" /> and the average height was 3.5 meters.<ref name="SWE" /> Their round, bean-shaped body terminated in a pointed tail.<ref name="SOTSR">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref> A pair of short,<ref name="LCATFOO" /> jointed arms<ref name="SOTSR" />&mdash;actually vestigial wings attached to the chest by membranes&mdash;<ref name="CSWE I 300" /> hung from their shoulders. These ended in four-fingered hands,<ref name="SOTSR" /> which lacked a great deal of manual dexterity.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> Quor'sav moved about on two long, stilt-like legs<ref name="CSWE III 65" /> with knobby knees<ref name="KC CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Kal'Falnl C'ndros}}</ref> that bent backward like a bird's.<ref name="SOTSR" /> Their feet were scaly. Members of the species could be powerfully muscled,<ref name="CSWE I 300" /> some to such an extent that other beings found them grotesque.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> This strength allowed their long legs to kick with devastating force, and their long neck and sharp beak to peck with penetrating results, although this left the Quor'sav vulnerable to counterattack.<ref name="SOTSR" />

A long, straight neck extended from the bulbous body at a roughly 45-degree angle.<ref name="SOTSR" /> Despite its length, the neck was not particularly flexible, and the head could not be tucked under the arm in the manner of many bird species.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> The neck supported a small, round head.<ref name="SOTSR" /> Their visage, though mostly static, featured a few mutable areas. Two large, blue<ref name="LCATFOO" /> eyes were situated to either side of the head,<ref name="SOTSR" /> protected by blinking eyelids.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> A downward-curving, pointed,<ref name="SOTSR" /> orange<ref name="CSWE I 300" /> beak stuck out between them,<ref name="SOTSR" /> pierced by two small, round nostrils.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> Wattles grew both between the eyes and under the beak.<ref name="SOTSR" /> Some members of the species had high, squeaky voices that other beings found annoying.<ref name="LCATFOO" />

With the exception of the legs,<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> the body was covered in a layer of down<ref name="LCATFOO" /> and an outer layer of yellow feathers.<ref name="CSWE I 300" /> The plumage of the arms was particularly thick,<ref name="LCATFOO" /> and that on the top of the head relatively long. Despite their natural covering, Quor'sav often wore clothing tailored to their unique body plan. Some, for example, had customized [[Flight suit/Legends|flight suits]]<ref name="SOTSR" /> and [[Environment suit/Legends|environment suits]].<ref name="LCATFOO" />

Quor'sav females laid several [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] upon fertilization. The eggs took more than a standard year to hatch.<ref name="SOTSR" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Yes, I'll have another centipede, Mother, if you don't mind!|Waywa Fybot, during a vivid dream|<ref name="classification" />}}
Quor'sav hailed from [[Uaua/Legends|Uaua]], the major [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Ua system]] in the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]] region of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], and a world notorious for its pesky [[Insect/Legends|insects]].<ref name="CGTTC">{{GamerCite|5|A Campaign Guide to the Centrality}}</ref> Their region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] was thinly inhabited, with average populations of fewer than one million sentients per inhabited world in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The Quor'sav [[Waywa Fybot]] lived in a town with homes built of [[Cement/Legends|cement]] and [[Steel/Legends|steel]] beams and covered with roofs of thatched straw, although synthetic materials had grown common there too. Fybot's home featured a lawn of magenta [[Grass/Legends|grass]] tended by domesticated [[Lawn louse|lawn lice]]. Individual properties in his neighborhood were separated by fences.<ref name="LCATFOO" />

They were nervous and anxious by nature,<ref name="CSWE I 300" /> yet proud of their avian heritage and willing to shrug off jibes aimed at their large size or strange appearance.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> Members of the species were wary of non-avians<ref name="CGTTC" /> and reserved special insults for mammalian species&mdash;especially for [[Primate/Legends|primates]] like [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="LCATFOO" />

Quor'sav mothers were known for their protective natures. Their eggs took more than a standard year to hatch, during which time the mother carefully guarded and protected them from predators and other dangers. This behavior was prevalent even in childless females; many Quor'sav took on a matronly persona when around friends whom they perceived as small and vulnerable. This could result in misunderstandings and annoyance for friends who did not wish to be babied, but it reassured and calmed strangers.<ref name="SOTSR" />

Quor'sav could manipulate their feathers to express emotion and aid communication. One greeting used by the species was to wave their arms and ruffle their feathers. Smooth and still feathers indicated calmness, those set erect expressed surprise or shock, and those shaking indicated extreme anger. Portions of the face could be altered to express emotion. For example, scrunching up the face in what appeared to be a grimace was a sign of joy. Quor'sav could speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]].<ref name="LCATFOO" /> They tended to take two-part names such as [[Kal'Falnl C'ndros]]<ref name="KC CCG" /> and Waywa Fybot.<ref name="CSWE I 300" />

The species had access to advanced technology, although much of this was customized for their unique anatomy. For example, Quor'sav preferred perch-like [[seating rack]]s, which looked like distorted chairs, and [[resting rack]]s, which resembled a pair of [[sawhorse]]s. They found perching on this latter device to be reassuring and comforting. Nevertheless, a Quor'sav in this position risked drowsiness and falling asleep.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> Their [[Starship/Legends|starships]], in particular, had to be custom-built and modified to allow for their large frames to operate comfortably.<ref name="SWE" />

Quor'sav cuisine was considered unappetizing to Humans. Nevertheless, some members of the species took cooking very seriously and became professional chefs. Quor'sav ate various creatures, including [[Centipede/Legends|centipedes]]<ref name="LCATFOO" /> and [[Nerf/Legends|nerfs]]. The dish [[Quor'sav-fried steak]] and [[Egg/Legends|eggs]], for example, consisted of nerfsteak fried in a [[pom]] seed batter.<ref name="DAD 2" />

==History==
The Quor'sav evolved on Uaua, a [[Planet/Legends|world]] in the Ua system.<ref name="CGTTC" /> The species' ancestors were winged avians capable of flight. Eventually, the species' wings developed into hands capable of fine manipulation but no longer capable of generating lift. Much later, the species evolved sentience and mastered the use of stone tools. Their technology progressed until they eventually reached the same standards as much of the rest of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="LCATFOO" />

The Quor'sav made contact with the outside galaxy at some point between [[3956 BBY|3956]] and [[3000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> and their world became part of the remote<ref name="CGTTC" /> region known as the Centrality. Such extra-planetary contact opened the door to colonists from other worlds, and alien settlers, many from mammalian species,<ref name="CSWE III 275">{{CSWECite|III|275}}</ref> arrived on Uaua. They were accompanied by another colonizer: a deadly [[virus]] to which mammals were immune but avians were susceptible. After a plague ravaged their world, the Quor'sav came to distrust and shun non-avian visitors to Uaua. The experience also sowed anti-Centrality sentiment among the population.<ref name="CGTTC" />

As with the rest of the Centrality, Uaua remained independent from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="CGTTC" /> The world fell within the domain of the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]] from [[1004 BBY|1004]] to [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], and the Quor'sav remained neutral during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="TEA" />

At least some Quor'sav emigrated from the world to take up residence on Republic planets. In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Quor'sav had moved to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], for example.<ref name="HNN49" /> With the [[Rise of the Empire era|rise of the Empire]], Uaua suffered from the general economic malaise that affected the Centrality as a whole. Uaua and the Centrality joined the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in exchange for monetary aid and the promise of autonomy. The region's fortunes improved under the new regime.<ref name="CGTTC" />

With the Empire's downfall at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Uaua and the Centrality were once again independent. The region signed goodwill treaties with the nascent [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] but remained suspicious of the new government and resisted overtures to join it. The economy once again suffered as the lack of Imperial buyers for goods took its toll. As the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] raged throughout the New Republic from [[25 ABY/Legends|25]] to [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]], the Centrality carefully built up its military and took in New Republic refugees, but did its best to stay out of the conflict.<ref name="CGTTC" /> Years later, Uaua fell within the bounds of [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Quor'sav in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Are you listening to me, you absurd collection of flightless feathers? Very well, then, and you can inform your mercantile-class sponsors that I gave you this direct order: you may arrest Bohhuah Mutdah, I haven't the power to stop you. But you will return him to me, alive and in condition to stand trial in the Oseon, or I'll have you plucked, dressed, and roasted for Founder's Day. Am I making myself clear?|Lob Doluff, to Waywa Fybot|<ref name="classification" />}}
[[File:Kalfalnl-cndros.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Kal'Falnl C'ndros]] (legs pictured) was a freelance Quor'sav pilot.]]
As early as 22 BBY, Quor'sav could be found as far from Uaua as the middle-class [[CoCo Town/Legends|CoCo District]] of Coruscant.<ref name="HNN49" /> Quor'sav in the greater galaxy faced prejudice and discrimination from Humans and similar species, who often made jokes about the species' size, appearance, and avian heritage.<ref name="LCATFOO" /> They had to stay alert for ovivorous species such as [[Yam'rii/Legends|Yam'rii]], for whom Quor'sav eggs were an irresistible treat.<ref name="SW:TSC">''[[Star Wars: The Saga Collection]]''</ref>

During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], at least some Quor'sav left their homeworld to enter Imperial service as part of a mandatory [[Unidentified treaty|conscription program]]. Waywa Fybot left Uaua in this way and became a narcotics agent for the Empire, despite his own ambitions to be a chef. In [[4 BBY/Legends|4 BBY]], Fybot struck a deal with a man who called himself [[Bohhuah Mutdah/Legends|Bohhuah Mutdah]] to deliver the Human gambler [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]; in exchange, Mutdah promised to relieve Fybot of his duty to the Empire. Meanwhile, Fybot's superior officer, [[Lob Doluff]], pressed Calrissian to go along with the Quor'sav and a Human agent named [[Bassi Vobah]] so that Calrissian might arrange a fake drug deal and the Quor'sav and Human might nab Mutdah. Fybot betrayed his true loyalties when he sabotaged Calrissian's [[Environment suit/Legends|environment suit]] and shot Bassi Vobah on [[Oseon 5792]]. Nevertheless, Fybot was himself betrayed when Bohhuah Mutdah revealed himself to be [[Rokur Gepta]], a [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerer of Tund]], and killed the avian.<ref name="LCATFOO" />

Other Quor'sav-at-large, such as Kal'Falnl C'ndros, operated independently. C'ndros worked as a pilot-for-hire from her base of operations, a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] known as the ''[[Shelltooth]]'',<ref name="SOTSR" /> custom-modified with high ceilings to fit her giant frame. C'ndros was known for her matronly demeanor and protectiveness,<ref name="SWE" /> traits that endeared her to clients but sometimes annoyed friends. C'ndros often took [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] runs to help with the costs of raising her many children.<ref name="SOTSR" /> On one of these trips, C'ndros visited the planet [[Yuvern/Legends|Yuvern]] and took the [[Yuvernian/Legends|Yuvernian]] [[Cane Adiss/Legends|Cane Adiss]] under her wing. The two traveled to dozens of worlds as C'ndros taught her apprentice the ins and outs of starship piloting. In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the duo parted ways on Tatooine.<ref name="CA DB">{{DB|character|caneadiss|Adiss, Cane}}</ref> C'ndros was present in Mos Eisley on the same day [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] sold his [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] to the [[Vuvrian/Legends|Vuvrian]] dealer [[Wioslea/Legends|Wioslea]].<ref name="ANH" /> Her presence in the spaceport came to the attention of the [[Yam'rii/Legends|Yam'rii]] [[Kitik Keed'kak]], who soon became obsessed with finding and eating the eggs<ref name="KK DB">{{DB|character|kitikkeedkak|Keed'kak, Kitik}}</ref> C'ndros had on her ship.<ref name="SWE" /> Three years later, C'ndros was among the smugglers given part of a cargo by the [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] [[Mal Biron]] on the planet [[Sriluur/Legends|Sriluur]] as part of a race to see who would receive a more lucrative cargo later. Working solo at this time and with another clutch of eggs to protect, she sought to team up with other participants.<ref name="SOTSR" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|So when Kevin sent comments during one of our edit sessions, he sent a note that said basically "You don't need this." And he was absolutely right.|Dan Wallace's recollection of Kevin J. Anderson's reaction to attempts to identify Waywa Fybot as a Quor'sav in ''The Essential Chronology''|<ref name="NJOE">{{WebCite|url=http://www.njoe.com/2009/05/03/dan-wallace-interview|text=Dan Wallace Interview|date=2009-05-03|author=Acky12|work=[http://www.njoe.com New Jedi Order Encyclopedia]|archivedate=20090523153847}}</ref>}}
[[File:LostCutStiltMonster-MOSW.png|thumb|right|A scene featuring a pair of possible Quor'sav legs (silhouette pictured) was cut from ''A New Hope''.]]
A pair of stilt-like legs appear briefly in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], released in [[1977]]; the legs walk across the screen from right to left in the scene where Luke Skywalker sells his speeder in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]].<ref name="ANH" /> Similar legs appear in the manga adaptation of [[Star Wars Manga: A New Hope|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'']], published in [[1998]], as Luke Skywalker and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] enter Mos Eisley. It is unclear whether these are supposed to belong to the same creature as shown in the film or another member of the same species.<ref name="Star Wars Manga: A New Hope">''[[Star Wars Manga: A New Hope]]'' 2</ref>

The legs went unnamed until [[1995]], when [[Decipher]]'s ''[[Premiere Limited]]'' set of cards for the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] identified them as belonging to Kal'Falnl C'ndros, a member of the Quor'sav species. The card reveals a few details about the unseen body above, describing the Quor'sav as tall avian&ndash;monotreme hybrids. Keeping with her large size, the game allows C'ndros to move further per turn than most other characters, but it forbids her to enter starships.<ref name="KC CCG" /> Another card, that of the Yam'rii character [[Kitik Keed'kak]], establishes the notion that Quor'sav must be alert for egg-eating predators and will defend their brood fiercely. The card's rules stipulate that Keed'kak is immediately lost if she finds herself at the same location as C'ndros.<ref name="KK CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Kitik Keed'kak}}</ref>

Six years after the release of ''A New Hope,'' [[L. Neil Smith]] included a tall, birdlike character named Waywa Fybot in his novel ''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]''. Fybot's species is never identified in the book, although several details about his homeworld and culture are detailed. Author [[Daniel Wallace|Dan Wallace]] attempted to identify Fybot as a Quor'sav while writing [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] with [[Kevin J. Anderson]]. Nevertheless, Anderson edited out Wallace's [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] as unnecessary.<ref name="NJOE" /> In [[2001]], [[Michael Kogge]] named the Quor'sav homeworld and placed it in the Centrality, the location of Smith's novel.<ref name="CGTTC" /> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' conclusively identified Fybot as a Quor'sav in [[2008]].<ref name="CSWE I 300" />

Later sources add extra details about C'ndros and the Quor'sav species. ''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]'', a supplement to ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' released by [[West End Games]] in [[1997]], contains the first and only image of a Quor'sav from the knees up. According to the game's rules, the Quor'sav's large size causes them to suffer penalties to attempts to hide and dodge. On the other hand, they move at 1.5 times the rate of a typical Human.<ref name="SOTSR" />

Other footage cut from ''A New Hope'' features another tall, stilt-legged creature that may be a Quor'sav. The fuzzy-legged, stubby-toed alien walks across the screen and scares the [[Bimm/Legends|Bimm]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Rycar Ryjerd/Legends|Rycar Ryjerd]] in the streets of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]]. The smuggler runs away, leaving the creature to stumble about perplexed.<ref name="Insider41">{{InsiderCite|41|The Evolution of Star Wars: Exploring the Lost Cut|The Evolution of ''Star Wars'': Exploring the Lost Cut}}</ref> The footage was shown as part of ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'', which aired on American television in [[1978]]. It is supposed to be part of the Imperial program "[[Life on Tatooine]]."<ref name="SWHS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref>
